clue.text: One language or another in which there's idle talk

indicators.note: the second language is said to hold the chatter within it, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: another language here is Malay, spoken in Malaysia
gas is informal for empty chatter

explanation.surface: A linguist muses on a tongue, or perhaps a different one, full of pointless chatter.
explanation.definitionFit: Malagasy is the national tongue of Madagascar, so it is one language among many.

clue.text: Jellyfish in America at bottom of sea

indicators.note: in a down entry, a piece placed at the bottom of another comes after it

parts.note: the Med is the Mediterranean Sea
USA is the United States of America

explanation.surface: A jellyfish is found off the American coast on the seabed.
explanation.definitionFit: A medusa is the free-swimming bell-shaped form of a jellyfish, so the word names that creature.

clue.text: Songs superior in sound

indicators.note: says the word for superior is heard rather than spelt, giving a similar-sounding entry

parts.note: a leader is someone superior, at the head of others

explanation.surface: Some songs are better when heard than read on the page.
explanation.definitionFit: Lieder are German art songs, such as those of Schubert, so the word is a plural for songs.

clue.text: Fresh garland's put on maiden getting clean sweep in contest

indicators.note: in a down entry, putting one piece on another places it above
a fresh version of the word is a new arrangement of its letters

parts.note: the possessive s is read as a letter of the fodder
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: A new floral wreath is placed on a girl who has won every event.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand slam is winning every event in a series, a total sweep of the competition, as in tennis or rugby.

clue.text: What may be spoilt by daisies and big rats?

definitions.text: What may be spoilt by daisies
definitions.meaning: excellent lawns, read as ..., can be marred by weeds such as daisies
rat is slang for an informer, and a supergrass is a major police informer

explanation.definitionFit: A supergrass is British slang for an informer who betrays many associates, a serious rat; read in two parts it suggests fine lawns.

clue.text: In that case, flights won't be covered

definitions.text: In that case, flights won't be covered

parts.words: In that case, flights won't be covered
parts.note: flights are the feathered ends of arrows; an archer's case for arrows leaves those ends sticking out of the top, uncovered

explanation.surface: Travel cover will not apply to air journeys in that situation.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests travel insurance; 'case' is really a container and 'flights' are arrow feathers.
explanation.definitionFit: A quiver is the archer's case for arrows, whose feathered flights poke out of its open end.

clue.text: Strong desires well up, beginning to end

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for well up is moved to the end

parts.note: to surge is to well up or rise in a rush

explanation.surface: Passions rise from the start right through to the finish.
explanation.walkthrough: SURGE with its S sent to the back gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Urges are strong impulses or cravings, so the plural noun matches strong desires.

clue.text: Six against a fast bowler of old in a test

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals
v is short for versus, meaning against
Bill Voce was an England fast bowler of the 1930s, famous in the Bodyline series

explanation.surface: In a cricket Test, six runs are scored against a veteran pace bowler.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket's 'Test' match is the surface; the answer is an oral examination.
explanation.definitionFit: A viva voce is an oral examination, often for a university degree, so it is a kind of test.

clue.text: What's left over from dinner may be put aside

definitions.text: What's left over from dinner may be
definitions.meaning: leftovers may be served up again
kept back or set apart for later use

explanation.definitionFit: Something reserved is kept back for later, and read as re-served it is food dished up a second time.

clue.text: A male about to come in silly or go out contented

indicators.note: one piece enters another, so it sits inside it

parts.note: dippy is informal for silly or scatty

indicators.note: the pieces A and male are turned round, read backwards

parts.note: he is a male person

explanation.surface: A man wonders whether to act foolishly or leave the party happy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses A and male, giving EHA; 'to come in' places that within the word for silly. 'or' is a link between the wordplay and the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To die happy is to pass away content, and go out is a euphemism for dying.

clue.text: Map makers collecting award for producing graphs

indicators.note: the map makers gather up the award, so it sits between their letters

parts.note: OS is the Ordnance Survey, Britain's national mapping agency
to award is to give

explanation.surface: Cartographers win a prize for drawing charts.
explanation.walkthrough: OS is the Ordnance Survey, which makes Britain's official maps.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogive is a cumulative frequency graph in statistics, so the plural fits graphs.

clue.text: For instrument get secure inside information on pitch

indicators.note: in a down entry one piece placed on another sits above it
the word for secure goes within the word for information

parts.note: gen is British slang for information
to lock is to secure
a spiel is a sales pitch, a glib patter

explanation.surface: To get an instrument, lock in some inside knowledge about the sales pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: A glockenspiel is a percussion instrument of tuned metal bars struck with hammers.

clue.text: Small fruit containing soft drug

indicators.note: the fruit holds the letter for soft inside it

parts.note: a seed is a small fruit-like grain of a plant
p, piano, is the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: A tiny fruit has some mild narcotic inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Speed is slang for amphetamine, a stimulant drug.

clue.text: Wanderer collects two pounds and so invests for the future?

indicators.note: the wanderer gathers the other letters into its middle

parts.note: a rover is a wanderer
L is the abbreviation for a pound sterling, so two pounds is LL
taken as written

explanation.surface: A traveller picks up some cash and puts it away for later.
explanation.definitionFit: When an investment rolls over, it is reinvested on maturity, carrying money forward to the future.

clue.text: Abused Plutarch redeemed — purchase book

indicators.note: abused letters are mistreated and knocked out of shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A mistreated copy of Plutarch is reclaimed at a bookshop.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Abused' signals the anagram of all three words, PLUTARCH REDEEMED PURCHASE, 24 letters.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the French title of Proust's multi-volume novel, known in English as In Search of Lost Time.

clue.text: One nice Dr getting confused about glandular system

indicators.note: the letters get mixed up, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A pleasant doctor becomes muddled when discussing hormones.
explanation.walkthrough: 'getting confused' rearranges ONE NICE DR; 'about' is a link meaning concerning.
explanation.definitionFit: The endocrine system is the network of ductless glands that release hormones into the blood.

clue.text: Inflammation produced by port? Positive answer to question!

parts.note: Aden is a port city in Yemen
'it is' is a yes to a question such as 'is it?'

explanation.surface: A harbour town causes some swelling, and the answer is yes!
explanation.definitionFit: Adenitis is inflammation of a gland, especially a lymph node.

clue.text: Game drips set up? It's pots!

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the pieces read from the bottom upwards

parts.note: snap is a card game
wets are feeble people, drips

explanation.surface: Does a card game set up a trap for wimps? It's pot luck!
explanation.walkthrough: One indicator, 'set up', turns both pieces together; the surface's 'set up' as a trap is the misdirection.
explanation.definitionFit: Stewpans are cooking pots used for stewing.

clue.text: See 14
Old coins showing sun on one side and wicked ruler on the other

parts.note: Sol is the sun, from the Latin
Idi Amin was the brutal dictator of Uganda

explanation.surface: Ancient coins bear the sun on the obverse and a tyrant's head on the reverse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on one side' and 'on the other' place SOL first and IDI second.
explanation.definitionFit: Solidi are gold coins of the late Roman and Byzantine empires, the plural of solidus.

clue.text: In which one may see mad gal posing naughtily?

definitions.text: In which one may see mad gal posing naughtily?

indicators.note: the letters strike a fresh pose, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A racy magazine shows a wild girl modelling saucily.
explanation.definitionFit: A lad mag is a magazine for young men, typically featuring risque photos of women.

clue.text: Two fresh from the match

parts.note: match is a marriage, not a game; a couple who have only just wed

explanation.definitionFit: Newlyweds are a recently married couple, two people straight from their wedding.

clue.text: Put up with volunteers in conference centre

indicators.note: in a down entry, up means the word is written bottom to top

parts.note: to lay something is to put it down
TA is the Territorial Army, Britain's volunteer reserve force

explanation.surface: Tolerate the volunteers at the conference venue.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads 'put up with' as tolerate; 'up' actually turns LAY into YAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Yalta in Crimea hosted the 1945 conference of Churchill, Roosevelt and Stalin.

clue.text: India's junior colt given exciting introduction to Academy

parts.note: c is an abbreviation for colt in horse-racing form
hot means exciting or sexy

indicators.note: the introduction to a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A young horse makes a thrilling debut at the academy.
explanation.definitionFit: Chota is an Anglo-Indian word from Hindi meaning small or junior.

clue.text: Around the room note botanical bits

indicators.note: the musical note goes around the room, enclosing it

parts.note: ti is a note of the sol-fa scale
a hall is a large room

explanation.surface: Around the room there is a note on plant parts.
explanation.definitionFit: Thalli are simple plant bodies without stems or leaves, as in algae and lichens.

clue.text: Surliness in speech as Far Eastern custom

indicators.note: spoken aloud, the word for surliness gives the entry by its sound

parts.note: cynicism here is a sour, sneering attitude

explanation.surface: Sourness in talk is given as a custom from the Orient.
explanation.definitionFit: Sinicism is a Chinese custom or idiom, from Sino- meaning Chinese.

clue.text: Walk in a particular way always behind band

indicators.note: the word for always follows the band

parts.note: a sash is a band of cloth worn over the shoulder
ay is an old word for always, also spelt aye

explanation.surface: Someone struts along forever at the back of the marching band.
explanation.definitionFit: To sashay is to walk in a showy, swaying manner.

clue.text: Transient love affair in which Peg is bowled over

indicators.note: the love affair holds the other piece within it

parts.note: a fling is a short love affair

indicators.note: the word for peg is knocked over, reading backwards

parts.note: a tee is the peg a golf ball sits on

explanation.surface: A brief romance in which Peg is swept off her feet.
explanation.walkthrough: Peg looks like a woman's name; it is a golf tee, turned to EET by 'bowled over'.
explanation.definitionFit: Fleeting means passing quickly, brief and transient.
